q: What is the CBAM default value for Indian steel structures, tanks and forgings?
title: CBAM default value: Indian steel structures
short: Indian steel structures and parts under CN 7308 carry 5.930 t CO2e per tonne. Large tanks under CN 7309 carry 6.650, gas cylinders under 7311 carry 6.640, and forged or stamped articles under 7326 carry 4.910. Direct emissions only, plus the 2026 mark-up.
audience: Indian fabricators, tank makers and forging units exporting steel articles to the EU

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7308 structures and parts of structures: 5.930
CN 7309 reservoirs and tanks over 300 litres: 6.650
CN 7310 tanks, drums and cans up to 300 litres: 4.310
CN 7326 forged, stamped and other articles: 4.910

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.

For a fabricator, almost all embedded emissions come from the plates, sections and tubes bought in. If your mill suppliers give verified figures, your actual value is their steel plus your cutting, welding and painting energy, which is small.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Default values definitive period (Excel, version 2 of 6 August 2026), India sheet; legally binding values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 correcting (EU) 2025/2621
European Commission, Guidance No. 3, CBAM methods for the calculation of emissions embedded in goods (14 August 2026), section 4.10
